actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species is endemic to Japan where it is distributed throughout Kyushu, Shikoku and Honshu and their adjacent islands including Goto Islands, Iki Island, and Osumi Islands (Tanegashima and Yakushima). There is an introduced population in western Hokkaido (Tokuda 2011, Suzuki et al. 2020) and it has also been introduced to Sado Island and the Izu Islands (Izu Oshima, Niijima, and Miyakejima). It occurs from sea level up to 2,500 m asl.
documentation.population: The population is decreasing especially in urban areas (Asaka et al. 2017), but is still common in mountainous regions. Overall, it is not in significant decline.
documentation.habitats: This species occurs in a wide variety of habitats ranging from coastal areas to high mountains. It breeds in still water where the larvae also develop. There is a wide geographic variation in the breeding season, ranging from October to May. A female can lay between 640-14,000 eggs. It can also be found in anthropogenic habitats.
documentation.threats: Infrastructure development for human settlement including the construction of roads are the main threats. Predation pressure from some introduced predators like racoons (Procyon lotor) might also be additional threats. There is a report suggesting that urban illumination may be harmful for the reproduction of this species (Ishiguro and Iwai 2018).
documentation.measures:
Conservation Actions In-Place
Its range includes several protected areas.

Research Needed
In the western subspecies (B. j. japonicus), there are two major genetic groups (Kyushu populations and others) which form a trichotomy with B. torrenticola (Igawa et al. 2006). Further taxonomic research is needed to resolve this status.
documentation.use_trade: This species is traded on the internet as a pet.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution, tolerance of a broad range of habitats, large population, and because it is unlikely to be declining fast enough to qualify for listing in a more threatened category.
documentation.taxonomic_notes: There are two subspecies: Bufo japonicus japonicus and B.j. formosus.
